title: The Name my support
hook: the true Name is my support and satisfies every hunger (Anand, opening pauris)

segments.voice: Yesterday, ghar terai, and your line, nothing is missing. This week: Chaupai closed with keep me, then Anand began: bliss together, anand bhaiaa, joy mother, stay with him, nothing is missing. Today, pauri four.

Ever eaten a whole meal and still felt hungry? Not stomach hungry. The other kind. You finish dinner and find yourself opening the fridge again, or scrolling for something to buy, or reaching for a phone with nothing new on it. There's a hunger food doesn't touch, and people feed it all day with whatever's nearest, and it never quite fills. The fourth pauri of Anand Sahib names something it says fills that hunger, all of it, with a word that also means what a building stands on.
screen: `A WHOLE MEAL, STILL HUNGRY.` → `THE FRIDGE, THE SCROLL, THE PHONE.` → `A HUNGER FOOD DOESN'T TOUCH.`

segments.voice: The pauri begins and ends with one line: saachaa naam meraa aadhaaro. The true Name is my support. Aadhaar means support, foundation, the base a thing rests on; the same word names India's national identity number today. In the pauri it's the ground under your feet. Then, in paraphrase: it has taken away all my hunger. It brought peace and calm to live in my mind, and fulfilled all my longings. I am forever a sacrifice to the Guru, who gives such greatness. Says Nanak, listen, saints: love the Word. Three things to notice. First, hunger. Bhukh is the plain everyday word, the hunger before lunch, and the pauri says the Name takes away all of it: a bold claim, made from experience, not as theory. Second, the order. Support first, then hunger gone, then peace comes to live in the mind. Peace isn't chased; it moves in once the foundation is there. Third, kurbaan, sacrifice: to give yourself wholly, the word people use when they'd do anything for someone. The joy of the first three pauris turns here into gratitude so full it wants to give itself away. And the pauri doesn't tell you to stop eating or stop wanting. It describes what happens when the deepest hunger is met: the smaller hungers lose their power. You're fed underneath.
screen: `AADHAAR: SUPPORT, FOUNDATION.` · `THE NAME TAKES AWAY ALL HUNGER.` · `THEN PEACE MOVES INTO THE MIND.` · `KURBAAN: GRATITUDE THAT GIVES ITSELF.` · then, large: `MY SUPPORT.`

segments.voice: If there's something to eat nearby, a piece of fruit or a sip of tea, take one bite now, or keep this for your next meal. Taste it fully, chew slowly, and notice the moment your body says, that's good. If you pray, you can say Waheguru first, the way many Sikhs remember the Name before eating; if not, just let the bite be enough.
Aadhaar, support or foundation. Saachaa naam meraa aadhaaro: the true Name is my foundation, and it takes away all hunger, so peace can come and live in the mind.
Your line: my support. A foundation holds up the whole house without being seen. That's day three hundred eighty-five.

howItsDone: Many Sikhs recite this fourth pauri as part of the short Anand Sahib at the close of services, and many remember the Name, saying Waheguru or a short prayer, before eating.

options: the true Name, my support: it takes away all hunger.

original.note: Gurmukhi: aadhaar, support or foundation; in pauri four, the true Name is my support.

trapdoor: what you thought: a pious line about God being important.
what it means: the true Name as the foundation you stand on, which meets the deepest hunger, so peace can move in.
what a scholar hears: aadhaar, from Sanskrit for that which holds up, is paired with bhukh, the plain word for hunger, and the pauri is framed by its own refrain, a common shape in Anand.

chat.says: What does 'the true Name is my support' even mean? Support for what?
options: Aadhaar means foundation: with the Name beneath you, deep hunger goes and peace moves in.
It means saying the Name brings in money, so you'll never go short or hungry again.
It means you should stop eating and stop wanting things if you want to grow spiritually.
chat.meaning: Saachaa naam meraa aadhaaro: the true Name is my foundation. It takes away all hunger, and then peace comes to live in the mind.
